rules.verified: The frozen prediction materially occurred within its original geography, hazard, severity threshold and target window.
rules.partial: Only part of the frozen prediction verified; geography, timing or severity may not fully match.
rules.falseAlarm: The prediction window matured without the specified event occurring.
rules.missedEvent: A significant observed disaster occurred without a qualifying frozen prediction beforehand.
rules.coverageFailure: A significant observed disaster occurred in a geography/hazard the scanner did not properly evaluate.

verifications.summary: Extreme rainfall and meaningful flood-related disruption occurred inside the frozen corridor, including damaged homes in Hue and agricultural impacts in Da Nang and Quang Ngai. The strongest destructive flooding and landslide impacts were outside the frozen corridor in Quang Tri, so the forecast is not upgraded to a full verification.
Window matured without independently verified material wildfire impacts satisfying the frozen outlook. The pre-existing GDACS fire signal is not counted as verification.

The frozen window matured at 08:00 ICT on 17 September without independently verified material flood impacts satisfying the outlook after the immutable freeze. Thai TMD/ONWR/DDPM warnings during the window are warnings, not observed-event verification. GDACS lists a Thailand flood dated 18 September, outside the frozen window, so it cannot be used retrospectively as a hit.

Window matured without sufficiently specific independent evidence of a new material flood event matching the frozen coordinates/geography and threshold after the immutable freeze. Rainfall warnings and relief activity for earlier Assam flooding are not treated as verification of this frozen outlook.

Window matured without a qualifying new material flood event matching the frozen geography/window after the immutable freeze. Continuing consequences and body recovery from the catastrophic 26 August Bhote Koshi disaster are post-event aftermath and cannot verify this later signal-derived outlook.

Window matured without independently verified material flooding matching the frozen outlook after the immutable freeze. Kenyan reporting in the period concerned preparedness for anticipated El Nino rains and light-to-moderate showers, not a qualifying observed flood disaster.

observedEvents.region: Northern and north-central Viet Nam: Lao Cai, Phu Tho, Ha Noi, Ninh Binh, Thanh Hoa and Nghe An
observedEvents.authoritativeSource: Viet Nam Government News / National Civil Defence Steering Committee and Department of Dyke Management and Disaster Prevention and Control
observedEvents.impacts: Material escalation confirmed by national reporting on 17 September: human casualties were reported; more than 16,300 homes were inundated across the affected provinces; flooding and landslides disrupted roads and rail; rivers in Ha Noi, Ninh Binh and Thanh Hoa exceeded alert level 3. Department figures reported by Vietnamese national media specify 3 deaths in a landslide in Da Bac, Phu Tho, 16,310 homes inundated, 4 houses collapsed, 29 damaged, and 22,499 ha of rice/crops/vegetables inundated or damaged.
observedEvents.forecastComparison: No qualifying frozen pre-event prediction was found in the immutable outlook ledger for this northern/north-central geography and event window. ND-001 is excluded because its frozen geography was the Hue-Da Nang corridor and its target window ended on 16 September. Signal-derived, aftershock, warning-derived, post-event and retrospective benchmark records are not eligible for independent prospective prediction credit.
observedEvents.coverageReason: The repository contains no immutable scan ledger in data/, so this event cannot yet be truthfully separated into SCANNED_BUT_NOT_FORECAST versus NOT_SCANNED/COVERAGE_FAILURE.
observedEvents.materialChange: Impact severity increased materially from the initial morning assessment: later national reporting established casualties and a much larger inundation footprint. Classification remains FALSE_NEGATIVE_UNPREDICTED_EVENT; this is an impact update, not a duplicate new event.

observedEvents.region: Bhote Koshi / Trishuli corridor; Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and downstream affected districts
observedEvents.hazard: Glacial flood / Flash flood / Debris flow / Landslide
observedEvents.authoritativeSource: Government of Nepal Ministry of Home Affairs / NDRRMA
observedEvents.impacts: Government of Nepal confirms the major Bhote Koshi flood began at 08:40 local time on 26 August and caused heavy loss of life and property in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Gorkha. NDRRMA's 17 September update, as reported by Nepal News and other outlets, gives 1,410 deaths, 6,145 people missing and 13,756 rescued in Nepal.
observedEvents.forecastComparison: No qualifying frozen prediction predating the 26 August onset was found in the immutable outlook ledger. The Nepal flood outlook OUT-gdacs-FL-1104157 was issued on 14 September for a 14-17 September window and was explicitly derived from an already-active GDACS flood signal, so it is post-event and receives no prospective prediction credit.
observedEvents.coverageReason: The repository contains no immutable scan ledger in data/, so the August 26 event cannot be truthfully separated into SCANNED_BUT_NOT_FORECAST versus NOT_SCANNED/COVERAGE_FAILURE.
observedEvents.materialChange: New historical coverage/forecast gap established in the accuracy ledger. The disaster itself began on 26 August; this record is newly added because the authoritative impact scale and absence of a qualifying pre-event frozen prediction were reconciled in this audit run.

scan.coverageLimitation: This engine evaluates what the providers below publish. There is no global cell-by-cell scan, and no claim is made about hazards outside each provider’s stated reach. A place absent from every provider was not examined and must not be read as quiet.

gdacs.label: GDACS (Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System)
gdacs.coverageResolution: Only events GDACS itself raises to an alert level. Flood, drought and wildfire records describe alert areas, not incident points.
gdacs.completenessBasis: GDACS lists only events it raises to an alert level, so a disaster it does not carry may simply be below that threshold.
gdacs.inputBasis: GDACS raises alerts on events it has already detected, so its records say what is happening rather than what will.

usgs.label: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program
usgs.coverageResolution: Every earthquake of magnitude 2.5 or above in the past seven days, at its epicentre. Anything smaller, or older, is outside this feed.
usgs.completenessBasis: A complete catalogue of earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 and above for the past seven days, so an absence above that threshold is meaningful.
usgs.inputBasis: A catalogue of earthquakes that have occurred.

emsc.label: EMSC (European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre)
emsc.geographicCoverage: Global, with the densest network in Europe and the Mediterranean
emsc.coverageResolution: Earthquakes of magnitude 4.5 or above, at epicentre.
emsc.inputBasis: A catalogue of earthquakes that have occurred.

eonet.label: NASA EONET
eonet.coverageResolution: A curated set of events drawn from Earth-observation sources. EONET does not claim to list every event, so absence here is not evidence of absence.
eonet.completenessBasis: A curated set; EONET does not claim to list every event, so its silence is not evidence.
eonet.inputBasis: A curated catalogue of natural events already under way.

nhc.label: NOAA National Hurricane Center
nhc.geographicCoverage: Atlantic, eastern Pacific and central Pacific basins only
nhc.coverageResolution: Active tropical cyclones, at storm centre. Storms in the western Pacific, Indian Ocean and southern hemisphere are outside this provider entirely.
nhc.completenessBasis: Every active tropical cyclone in the basins it publishes for.
nhc.inputBasis: The hurricane centre publishes advisories for active systems, including where a storm is expected to go, which is an input to a forecast of what it has not yet done.

nws.label: NOAA / National Weather Service
nws.geographicCoverage: United States and its territories only
nws.coverageResolution: Alerts at severe or extreme severity, carrying the affected-area polygon where the agency published one and a forecast-zone centre where it did not.
nws.completenessBasis: Exhaustive for active warnings, but a warning is not an observation: these records never enter the observed-disaster ledger, so this provider cannot establish that no disaster occurred.
nws.inputBasis: A watch or warning states that severe weather is expected, which is a statement about what has not happened yet.

reliefweb.label: ReliefWeb (UN OCHA)
reliefweb.coverageResolution: Country-level humanitarian disaster declarations. These carry no incident coordinates and are placed at a country centroid.
reliefweb.completenessBasis: Only disasters ReliefWeb has declared, which is a subset of those that occur.
reliefweb.inputBasis: Situation reports and declarations published after a disaster has occurred.

usgs_volcano.label: USGS Volcano Hazards Program
usgs_volcano.geographicCoverage: Volcanoes monitored by the United States volcano observatories
usgs_volcano.coverageResolution: Volcanoes currently at an elevated alert level. Volcanoes outside the US observatory network are not covered by this provider.
usgs_volcano.completenessBasis: Exhaustive for elevated alert levels in the observatory network it covers, which is not the same as exhaustive for eruptions that caused harm: an alert level is a published status, these records never enter the observed-disaster ledger, and their silence establishes only that nothing was elevated.
usgs_volcano.inputBasis: A volcano alert level states expected activity - a watch or warning is issued for unrest before an eruption, not after it.

scan.providerVersionNote: Each scan records the provider definitions in force when it ran, under providerVersions. A definition is never applied backwards: widening a provider’s scope or calling it exhaustive changes what future scans can establish, never what past ones did.

retention.note: Per-scan detail is held for the most recent 2000 scans. Coverage before detailFrom cannot be established from this ledger and must be reported as DATA_UNAVAILABLE, never as scanned or unscanned.

backtest.note: Hindcast by tools/backtest-models.js: forecasts Open-Meteo really issued 3 and 5 days ahead, corrected as the live run corrects them with only the measurements available at issue time, scored day by day against NASA POWER. It shows how the method behaves; it is not the record of published forecasts.
backtest.fireNote: Fire is scored with the index codes carried from at least 30 days of measured weather to the day before, and the forecast used for the day itself only.

modelVerdicts.note: How each published model forecast turned out, by tools/run-models.js: correct if its weather line was crossed on at least one day of its window, a false alarm if not, pending until every day has been measured by NASA POWER. A miss is a day the line was crossed at a place a published run was watching, with no forecast for it.
